question: Salesforce AMTS (new grad) Technical Interview 2: **implement an LRU cache from scratch as production-ready OOP code** (class design, separation of responsibilities, time and space complexity), then **extend it to an LFU cache**. This pair was reported across AMTS, MTS and SMTS loops in 2025-26; in one MTS virtual round both were asked and solved with working code, and in one onsite drive LRU alone was the elimination round.
lookingFor: O(1) get and put via the right combination of data structures.
Clean OOP: encapsulation, generics, small interfaces, error handling.
Pointer-handling correctness (doubly linked list updates, sentinels).
Ability to extend a design: from recency to frequency with tie-breaks.
Testing, edge cases and complexity analysis.
followUps: Why a doubly linked list rather than a singly linked list or an array?
How would you make the cache thread-safe without a global lock?
How would you add TTL expiry to the cache?
How does LFU behave with a burst of old popular keys, and how can you fix it (aging)?
How would you scale it as a distributed cache?
